rv.q: At the centre of it all, Marsh is a wildly entertaining presence, a gangly man who, thanks to nimble rhymes and physical clowning, can go from tender to Mach 1 in the space of a couplet.
It might not, to paraphrase the soundtrack’s most iconic song, take one’s breath away, but it is a solidly entertaining hour of nostalgic whimsy.
Top Gunchained is poignant, hectic, non-stop, funny and, most of all, a great night out.
With an against-the-odds success entirely befitting his eighties action film models, he pulls it off.
That he does this with the help of mere paper planes, a single chair, a bit of audience karaoke and a carrot renders Marsh one of our great solo storytellers.
What initially appears to be a playful celebration of a much-loved film gradually reveals a poignant exploration of family, memory and the patterns we inherit.

cn.t: Richard Marsh's one-man verse retelling of Top Gun earns strong praise for its exhilarating storytelling and sharp wit. Critics highlight his expert performance and the show's emotional depth as standout strengths.
